The test image shows opened soybean pods with:
- Shriveled, dull, discolored seeds (brown, gray, tan)
- White/cottony fluffy material inside the pod cavity
- Seeds appearing cracked and poorly developed

Key candidates:
- **White Mold**: "white cottony seeds in pods" - matches the fluffy white material
- **Phomopsis**: "cracked, shriveled, dull seeds with gray mold" - matches seed appearance

The white cottony mycelium visible inside the pod cavity is the distinguishing feature — this is characteristic of White Mold (Sclerotinia). The reference image confirms white fluffy growth associated with this disease on pods/stems.
